scores.evidence: 'Morning' section opens 'If you only caught the last three laps on Sunday, you saw the pass' — narrates before evaluating; verdict-first only in some sections
'Until next week' paragraph restates standings and previews next race — explicit summary/wrap-up closure violating the rule
'Morning' section opens with 'If you only caught...' — a bridging/orienting sentence rather than letting the heading do transitional work
'0.85s a lap... 18 seconds... 31 seconds... 13.7s' cluster within the VSC section; several paragraphs pile multiple figures rather than deploying one surgically
'Would he have won anyway? I don't think so... it might not have' — explicit owned speculation; certainty reserved for documented outcomes
Russell is the constant benchmark throughout: lead times, tyre strategy, stop timing all measured against Russell before any absolute framing
'CAR 12 (ANT) TIME 1:28.582 DELETED - TRACK LIMITS AT TURN 1 LAP 49' — official message lands as hard stop complicating the pass narrative
'Leclerc went off on lap 2, race control called SAFETY CAR DEPLOYED and then RED FLAG' — recaps sequence rather than interpreting meaning
'Gasly (7th)... The car drifted back to where its race pace put it' — flat, dry recounting for comic/ironic deflation of Alpine's pole narrative
'Here's what the data does say' — meta-sentence about the piece itself; first-person judgment calls present but occasionally diluted by frame-setting prose
Names dropped without introduction, 'VSC', 'DRS', timing data, escape-road instructions cited without definition — fully peer-addressed throughout
'It was a conventional tyre split. It set up the rest of the afternoon.' — consistent two-to-four sentence paragraphs, each exiting cleanly
'Half a second a lap quicker wasn't enough to get past at Monza. / This is the bit the 19th-to-first line hides' — long analytical sentence answered by short punchy one
VSC section correctly peaks in density; 'Winners and losers' bullets compress everything equally regardless of significance, losing the density gradient

top_fixes: Kill 'Until next week' entirely — it is a summary paragraph with a standings restatement and a preview, violating S2 on both counts; the piece should end when the Pérez/Tsunoda entry closes

'Morning' section violates S1 and S3: drop 'If you only caught the last three laps...' and 'Here's what the data does say' — open on the evaluative claim about lap 3, not on an address to the reader or a meta-sentence about the piece

Thin the figure clusters in the VSC section — '13.7s behind the leader... about 31 seconds... 18 seconds cheaper' in two consecutive sentences dilutes E1; pick the one number that clinches the point (the 18-second delta) and let the others fall into subordinate clauses or be cut
